claims.text: This package supplies the contestants for the repo's tournaments: the same `vol run` configs that fit a single [[HAR]] baseline can field 13 models and compare them with statistical tests, so every design choice here is built to be raced, not admired.

cite.quote:
# Single-model experiment (ingest + train + evaluate + dashboard)
vol run --config workspace/configs/baseline_har.yaml

# Tournament: 13 models compared with statistical tests
vol run --config workspace/configs/tournament_full_spy.yaml
focus: # Tournament: 13 models compared with statistical tests

claims.text: The signature move: training loss equals evaluation loss, LightGBM's custom objective hands the booster the analytic [[QLIKE]] gradient 1 - exp(y_true - y_pred) and hessian exp(y_true - y_pred) in log-RV space, so trees split on the exact metric the tournament scores.

cite.quote:
def qlike_objective(y_pred: np.ndarray, dtrain: Any) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Custom QLIKE objective for LightGBM.

    Log-space QLIKE: L = exp(y_true - y_pred) - (y_true - y_pred) - 1
    gradient (dL/dy_pred) = 1 - exp(y_true - y_pred)

claims.text: The objective knows its data: log RV for these assets spans roughly -14 to -4, so the symmetric clip at plus or minus 10 is pure float64 overflow protection, with QLIKE's natural exponential already penalizing under-predicted volatility harder than over-predicted.

cite.quote:
# Symmetric clip: pure overflow protection. exp(709) overflows float64.
    # Data range is ~10 (log RV spans -14 to -4), so ±10 covers all cases.
    # QLIKE's natural exponential already penalizes under-prediction harder.
focus: # Data range is ~10 (log RV spans -14 to -4), so ±10 covers all cases.

claims.text: `xgboost` is the deliberate second opinion: an independent boosting library carrying the identical QLIKE gradient and hessian, so any LightGBM edge that fails to replicate there reads as a library artifact, not signal.

cite.quote:
def qlike_objective_xgb(y_pred: np.ndarray, dtrain: Any) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Custom QLIKE objective for XGBoost.

    Log-space QLIKE: L = exp(y_true - y_pred) - (y_true - y_pred) - 1
    gradient (dL/dy_pred) = 1 - exp(y_true - y_pred)
    hessian  (d²L/dy_pred²) = exp(y_true - y_pred)

claims.text: The graph family reframes forecasting across assets instead of across time: each trading date becomes one graph whose nodes are symbols and whose edges come from rolling correlation, and `requires_graph = True` routes these snapshots to the model instead of tabular features.

cite.quote:
Operates on graph snapshots: each date = one graph with N nodes
    (symbols) and edges from rolling correlation. Integrates with the
    feature_stack pipeline via extract_features().

    Set ``requires_graph = True`` so the pipeline runner can detect
    graph-mode and dispatch appropriately.

claims.text: The torch side makes the same commitment: graph models train on `_qlike_loss`, exp(y - y_hat) - (y - y_hat) - 1 in log-RV space with the same clamp at 10, so no family in the zoo gets to optimize a friendlier loss than the one it is judged on.

focus: QLIKE in log-RV space: exp(y - y_hat) - (y - y_hat) - 1

claims.text: Hyperparameter search respects time the same way the outer evaluation does: Optuna tunes over ExpandingWindowCV walk-forward splits to prevent look-ahead bias, and each worker process is pinned round-robin to its own GPU so 8 devices run all trials in parallel.

cite.quote:
"""Tune XGBoost hyperparameters via Optuna with walk-forward CV.

    Uses ExpandingWindowCV (walk-forward) to prevent look-ahead bias.
    Optimizes QLIKE loss with TPE sampler.

    When gpu_device_ids is provided, each worker is pinned to a separate
    GPU (round-robin). With 8 GPUs and 8 workers, all trials run in
    parallel on different devices.
focus: Uses ExpandingWindowCV (walk-forward) to prevent look-ahead bias.

claims.text: What the zoo does not do is judge itself: a model only emits log-RV predictions under the shared base contract, while fold construction, the Duan retransformation, QLIKE ranking and Diebold-Mariano testing all live outside this package.
